subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up. As it rises (before reaching the top), which energy transfer mainly occurs?
options: Chemical to kinetic
Gravitational potential to kinetic
Thermal to kinetic
Kinetic to gravitational potential
questions.explain: As the ball rises it slows down, so its kinetic store falls while its gravitational potential store rises: energy is transferred from kinetic to gravitational potential.

questions.q: What is the activity of a radioactive source?
options: The rate at which its nuclei decay, measured in becquerel (Bq)
The mass of the source
The energy of each emitted particle
The number of undecayed nuclei remaining
questions.explain: Activity is the rate at which nuclei of a source decay, measured in becquerel (Bq), where 1 Bq is one decay per second.

questions.q: Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
options: A sound wave in air
A wave on a string
A water wave
Light
questions.explain: Sound is a longitudinal wave: the air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer, creating compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: What happens to the average kinetic energy of gas particles as the temperature of the gas increases?
options: It decreases
It stays the same
It depends on the container size
It increases
questions.explain: The temperature of a gas is related to the average kinetic energy of its particles: raising the temperature increases their average kinetic energy, so they move faster.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an energy store?
options: Kinetic
Elastic potential
Current
Chemical
questions.explain: Current is a rate of flow of charge, not an energy store. The stores are kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, magnetic, electrostatic and nuclear.

questions.q: Which energy resource is most reliable for continuous large-scale electricity generation?
options: Wave
Fossil fuels
Wind
Solar
questions.explain: Fossil-fuel power stations can run on demand at any time, making them reliable, whereas solar, wind and wave depend on the weather and time of day.

questions.q: Why is a change of state described as a physical change rather than a chemical change?
options: A new substance is always made
Energy is destroyed during the change
The substance recovers its original properties if the change is reversed
The number of particles changes
questions.explain: Changes of state are physical: no new substance forms, and the material recovers its original properties if the change is reversed (e.g. water refreezing to ice).

questions.q: A house is insulated with material of low thermal conductivity. What is the main effect?
options: Energy is transferred through the walls faster
The house gains energy from outside
The walls become thinner
Energy is transferred through the walls more slowly
questions.explain: Lower thermal conductivity reduces the rate at which energy is transferred through the walls, so the building cools down more slowly.

questions.q: Why did scientists propose the existence of dark matter and dark energy?
options: Because the universe contains no ordinary matter
To explain observations (such as galaxy motion and accelerating expansion) that ordinary matter alone cannot account for
To replace the Big Bang theory
To explain the colour of stars
questions.explain: Observations of how galaxies move and how the universe's expansion is speeding up cannot be explained by visible matter alone, so scientists proposed dark matter and dark energy. There is still much we do not understand about them.

questions.q: In the national grid, what is the role of a step-down transformer near homes?
options: To lower the voltage to a safer level for domestic use
To increase the current in the transmission lines
To convert ac to dc
To raise the voltage for long-distance transmission
questions.explain: Step-up transformers raise the voltage for efficient transmission; step-down transformers near towns and homes lower the voltage (e.g. to 230 V) so it is safe to use in buildings.

questions.q: What is the role of a step-down transformer in the national grid?
options: It increases the p.d. before transmission
It converts ac to dc
It decreases the p.d. to a safe value for homes
It increases the current in the transmission cables
questions.explain: A step-down transformer reduces the high transmission potential difference to a safer, lower value (about 230 V) for use in homes. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. for transmission.

questions.q: What is the specific latent heat of vaporisation of a substance?
options: The energy to raise 1 kg by 1°C
The energy to melt 1 g of the substance
The energy to change the state of 1 kg from solid to liquid
The energy to change the state of 1 kg from liquid to gas with no temperature change
questions.explain: Specific latent heat of vaporisation is the energy needed to change 1 kg of a substance from liquid to gas (or back) at constant temperature. Latent heat of fusion refers to the solid↔liquid change.

questions.q: What is meant by the internal energy of a system?
options: The energy supplied by an external heater
Only the kinetic energy of the particles
The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles
Only the potential energy stored between particles
questions.explain: Internal energy is the total energy stored by the particles: the sum of their kinetic energy (from motion) and the potential energy stored in the bonds/forces between them.

questions.q: A child slides down a slide and ends up moving more slowly than a frictionless calculation predicts. Where has the 'missing' energy gone?
options: It has been destroyed
Dissipated as thermal energy by friction
Converted entirely to sound
Stored as extra chemical energy
questions.explain: Energy is conserved and cannot be destroyed. Friction dissipates energy to the thermal store of the slide and surroundings, so less reaches the kinetic store.

questions.q: What is a major environmental drawback of burning fossil fuels for electricity?
options: They cannot be transported
They release carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change
They produce radioactive waste
They use up the world's water
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) plus other pollutants, contributing to global warming and acid rain. Radioactive waste is a drawback of nuclear power, not fossil fuels.

questions.q: What makes a main sequence star (like the Sun) stable for billions of years?
options: It is held together by magnetism
The inward force of gravity is balanced by the outward pressure from fusion energy
It is constantly shrinking
There are no forces acting on it
questions.explain: During the main sequence the inward pull of gravity is balanced by the outward force from the expansion of hot gases (energy released by hydrogen fusion). This equilibrium keeps the star stable.

questions.q: In a transverse wave, how do the oscillations relate to the direction the wave travels (energy transfer)?
options: In the same direction as the energy
Perpendicular (at 90°) to the direction of energy transfer
There are no oscillations
Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer. In a longitudinal wave they are parallel to it.

questions.q: What was Bohr's key contribution to the development of the atomic model?
options: He fired alpha particles at gold foil
He proposed the plum pudding model
He suggested electrons orbit the nucleus at specific fixed distances (energy levels)
He discovered the proton
questions.explain: Bohr adapted the nuclear model by proposing that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances (energy levels), which matched experimental observations.

questions.q: Why does the national grid use step-up transformers before transmission over long distances?
options: To convert ac to dc for transmission
To increase the current and reduce the voltage
To make the cables thicker
To increase the voltage and reduce the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
questions.explain: Stepping up the p.d. reduces the current for the same power (P = VI). Lower current means much less energy wasted as heat in the resistance of the transmission cables (heating ∝ I²R).

questions.q: How did the Sun form?
options: From a black hole running out of energy
From the explosion of a planet
From a collapsing cloud of dust and gas (a nebula) pulled together by gravity
It has always existed unchanged
questions.explain: The Sun formed when a cloud of dust and gas (nebula) was pulled together by gravity. As it collapsed it heated up, eventually starting nuclear fusion.

questions.q: Why can the efficiency of a real device never be 100%?
options: Power and energy are different quantities
Some energy is always dissipated to less useful stores
Some energy is always destroyed
All devices store chemical energy
questions.explain: Energy is conserved, but some is always dissipated (e.g. as thermal energy through friction or heating), so useful output is always less than total input.

questions.q: Why does the national grid transmit electricity at very high potential difference and low current?
options: To make the current alternate faster
To increase the resistance of the cables
To increase the power generated
To reduce energy wasted as heat in the cables
questions.explain: Power loss in cables is given by P = I^2 R, so reducing the current greatly reduces energy wasted as heat. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. and lower the current for efficient transmission.
